title: Ordinary henselization as a limit of residue-preserving affine etale neighbourhoods
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $x\in X$ correspond to a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, with residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. There exist a henselian local $A$-algebra $H$ [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], a nonempty directed set $I$, and a directed system of $A$-algebras $A_a$ with colimit $H$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], such that each $u_a:\operatorname{Spec}A_a\to X$ is separated etale of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and has a chosen point $x_a$ over $x$ inducing an isomorphism $\kappa(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(x_a)$. The transition maps preserve these points and their residue-field identifications. The induced map $\operatorname{Spec}H\to\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ takes the closed point to $x_a$; the map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to H$ is local, $\mathfrak pH$ is the maximal ideal, and $\kappa(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}H/\mathfrak pH$. Moreover $\operatorname{Spec}H\cong\varprojlim_a\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ over $X$.
